verdicts.evidence: audit_claim1.py solves the adversarial problem as a finite LP across the complete 2-label/2-action integer-loss family plus 120 asymmetric 3-label cases and five alpha values; all 28,950 comparisons match the closed-form l_in + alpha*max(l_out-l_in,0) with max error 1.42e-14, and a destructive control confirms the out-of-set penalty changes the policy as predicted.

The logbook explicitly states this claim was not attempted; the finite discrete audits used for other claims do not satisfy the non-atomic feature-space assumption required for Proposition 3.1 and Theorem 3.3, and no experiments were run.

audit_claim3_exchangeability.py implements Algorithm 1 literally and exhaustively checks 14,850 exchangeability orbit/alpha combinations on a nine-observation support with worst coverage hitting the finite-sample bound to 1.11e-16; additionally, fresh empirical runs on 20 COVID seeds and 20 BDD splits show mean miscoverage within 0.00244 of alpha across seven alpha values.

Official cached probabilities were evaluated from scratch across COVID seeds 23-42 under both loss matrices, BDD seeds 23-42, seven alpha values, and six baselines; under high-cost Lambda1 ROCP achieves zero critical mistakes for all three medical labels versus RAC's nonzero rates, and on BDD ROCP realized loss is 2.320±0.019 vs RAC 2.981±0.075 with reduced collision rates across hazard states.

overall: The logbook provides concrete computational and empirical evidence supporting Claims 1, 3, and 4, including exhaustive LP verification of the minimax policy, exhaustive exchangeability checks plus empirical coverage tracking, and real-dataset evaluations showing reduced critical mistakes. Claim 2 is explicitly not addressed, as the required non-atomic continuous-setting duality theory was outside the audit's scope.
